moduleTitle: Additional Lesson - Managing TDS repositories using Tosca API
learningObjectives: Generate API Scan messages from the installed Test Data Service Swagger definition.
Distinguish repository administration from test-item operations and inspect the selected API version before sending requests.
Check the documented request schema, authentication and response before changing repository configuration.
Distinguish saving an API Scan project from exporting messages to Tosca Commander.

elements.description: A repository connects Test Data Service to a data store. Creating or changing its configuration is different from finding or updating an item within it. API Scan can also manage test data; item operations are not exclusive to the Standard Modules.

elements.text: This is an independent documentation-based workflow. The Academy video and its endpoint examples have not been verified. Use the Swagger definition of your installed service for exact methods, paths and payloads.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Generate the API Scan message tree

elements.description: On the Tosca Server machine, open the Test Data Service Swagger documentation and download swagger.json. Select Home > File in API Scan to load that definition. Check the base path before scanning it. The documented examples use API v2.

elements.text: The Gateway documentation address is http://<server address>:<port>/testdataservice/swagger/index.html. With an HTTPS binding, the documentation instructions instead use the local Test Data Service port on the server machine. Select a definition to inspect the desired API version.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Create a repository: inspect the contract

elements.description: Select the create operation in the installed Swagger definition and inspect its method, request schema and required fields. Do not assume a four-field SQLite example is valid for every database type.

elements.title: Repository configuration concepts
items: A repository needs a unique name; description is optional.
SQLite is file-backed; InMemory loses its data when the server restarts.
MSSQL and Oracle have database connection settings rather than simply a SQLite file location.

elements.text: For a JSON request body, use the media type declared by its API definition. A Content-Type header alone does not authenticate the request or grant repository permissions.

elements.description: In a disposable environment, prepare a repository named PracticeData using the installed schema. Inspect the response, then verify its configuration in Test Data Management. No successful API execution is claimed by this lesson.

Inspect the definition for the read operation, including whether it returns a collection or targets one repository. Use its documented path parameters and response schema. A collection address should not be assumed to return one named repository.

Use the installed API definition to identify the update contract; do not guess that it is the same as Create. In the documented Test Data Management editor, only Name and Description can be changed because other changes require migration.

elements.term: An edit is not a migration
elements.description: The web editor does not support editing InMemory repositories. These web UI limits do not establish a different API contract; consult the installed definition before automating configuration changes.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Delete a repository: check the data effect

elements.description: Deleting repository configuration must not be confused with erasing the underlying data. The documented web dialog has a separate Also delete database option for permanent database deletion. Inspect the equivalent API operation and parameters before using it.
Use only disposable practice data. Check the request target and response, then verify which configuration and data remain. A missing repository tile alone is not proof that its database was erased.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Save the project or export messages

elements.text: Home > Save as saves an API Scan project; Home > Open reopens one. API TestCase exports selected messages to Tosca Commander. These are separate operations: do not promise that Save as creates a .tsu subset importable into every workspace.

examPitfalls.title: Guessing endpoints from an old demonstration
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reusing a method, path or payload without checking the installed API version.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Generate messages from the installed Swagger definition and inspect the operation schema before sending.

examPitfalls.title: Treating headers as permission
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming application/json grants access to repository administration.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check the API security requirements and repository permissions as well as the declared request media type.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing saved artifacts and deleted data
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming Save as is a Commander subset export or that removing a repository always erases its database.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the appropriate project-save/export action and verify the deletion parameters and resulting data state.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Before automating repository administration in API Scan, where should a tester verify the exact HTTP method, path and payload for the installed Test Data Service version?

options.text: In an old video without checking its API version.
In the installed Test Data Service Swagger definition.
In the DELETE command, regardless of the desired operation.

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the definition supplied by the service you will call.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The installed Swagger definition describes the selected API version. Scan its swagger.json and inspect the relevant operation rather than guessing an endpoint from a demonstration.

optionExplanations.A: An old example may target a different API version and cannot establish the installed operation contract.
optionExplanations.B: The service exposes versioned Swagger documentation; its definition supplies the operation schema to inspect.
optionExplanations.C: DELETE concerns removal, not a universal contract for reading, creating or changing configuration.
optionExplanations.D: Tile appearance is a visual cue and does not describe HTTP methods, paths or request schemas.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A JSON repository request declares application/json as its required media type. What can happen if the tester omits Content-Type?

options.text: The request works exactly the same regardless of headers.
Without Content-Type: application/json, the JSON payload may not be interpreted correctly by the server.
The repository is created but immediately locked.
Headers are only required for DELETE requests.

practiceQuiz.hint: Media type and authorization solve different problems.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Omitting the declared JSON media type can prevent correct interpretation of the body. Supplying it does not itself grant repository access.

optionExplanations.A: A request body has a declared media type; headers cannot be dismissed as irrelevant.
optionExplanations.B: The missing JSON media type can cause incorrect body interpretation or rejection; inspect the response.
optionExplanations.C: Omitting a media-type header does not imply that a repository is created and locked.
optionExplanations.D: A JSON-bodied request needs its declared media type; this requirement is not exclusive to deletion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the scope of repository administration, as distinct from test-item operations?

options.text: Managing individual test records, the same as the TDS Standard Modules.
Managing whole TDS repositories themselves — creating, retrieving, updating, and deleting the repository.

practiceQuiz.hint: This lesson operates one level above individual test records.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Repository administration concerns the configured repository. Item-level operations concern its test data; API Scan can support those too.

optionExplanations.A: Finding or changing a test item is a different scope from configuring its containing repository.
optionExplanations.B: These are repository administration operations; database-data deletion remains a distinct effect to check.
optionExplanations.C: Repository administration does not manage Commander license keys.
optionExplanations.D: Requirements and RequirementSets are not Test Data Service repository configuration.

quickRecap.value: Use the installed versioned Swagger definition for methods, paths, bodies and responses.
Download swagger.json and scan it with API Scan Home > File; check the base path.
InMemory, SQLite, MSSQL and Oracle have different persistence and connection requirements.
The web editor changes Name and Description; an API contract must be checked separately.
Removing configuration and permanently deleting its database are distinct effects.
Save as saves an API Scan project; API TestCase exports messages to Commander.
